# Ensure Authorization header is available to PHP (useful for many shared hosts) # Try both methods as hosts vary in which directive they support.
# Method 1: pass through Authorization to HTTP_AUTHORIZATION env var RewriteEngine On RewriteRule .* - [E=HTTP_AUTHORIZATION:%{HTTP:Authorization}]
# Method 2: Set env if Authorization present (fallback) <IfModule mod_setenvif.c> SetEnvIf Authorization "(.*)" HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1 </IfModule>
# Optional: force JSON responses to avoid accidental HTML from PHP errors (disabled by default) # Header set Content-Type "application/json; charset=utf-8"

option.name: updatedContent
option.value:
# Ensure Authorization header is available to PHP (useful for many shared hosts) # Try both methods as hosts vary in which directive they support.
# Method 1: pass through Authorization to HTTP_AUTHORIZATION env var RewriteEngine On RewriteRule .* - [E=HTTP_AUTHORIZATION:%{HTTP:Authorization}]
# Method 2: Set env if Authorization present (fallback) <IfModule mod_setenvif.c> SetEnvIf Authorization "(.*)" HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1 </IfModule>
# Optional: force JSON responses to avoid accidental HTML from PHP errors (disabled by default) # Header set Content-Type "application/json; charset=utf-8"
# Prevent mod_rewrite in API folder so PHP endpoints are served correctly <IfModule mod_rewrite.c> RewriteEngine Off </IfModule>
# Disable directory listing Options -Indexes
# Ensure PHP files are handled by the server (most shared hosts already do this) <IfModule mod_mime.c> AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .php </IfModule>
